statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Tail is 6 of 100 in the low band, nineteen points below the 25-point block threshold, because the CME equity index futures halt is now twenty-seven hours old and removes the very price path this score measures; twenty-two of the twenty-four forward slots lie inside that closure. Stress holds at 57 in the elevated band: the Saudi East-West pipeline that normally carries 4% to 5% of global oil supply remains shut after Iraq-origin drone strikes, Houthi forces hold Perim island and the Bab el-Mandeb exit, and CME FedWatch pricing for a 25 basis point hike at Wednesday's FOMC stands near 87% after August core CPI printed 0.3% month over month against a 0.2% estimate. Confidence is 87 in the high band: the index level, VIX, the H.15 yield curve, crude, rate-hike pricing, the seven-day calendar and the Red Sea sequence were each re-verified against primary sources this hour, and the only structurally unavailable input is live price path.
recommendation: Tail sits deep in the low band, so the deterministic mapping returns EA_ON and a green status, and this single shared reading applies jointly to NQ futures and NAS100 CFD. Three observations support it. First, no venue quotes the Nasdaq-100 in twenty-two of the twenty-four published forward slots: CME equity index futures halted at 21:00 UTC on Friday and reopen at 22:00 UTC on Sunday, so a score that measures a pathological price path cannot be elevated across hours in which no path can form. Second, the last observed session granted mean reversion rather than denying it, and did so against a hawkish input: August CPI printed with core slightly hot and hike odds jumped to roughly 87%, yet the index still closed 29,368.44, up 264.93 points or 0.91%, about 105 points below its 29,473.12 high inside a 159.61-point range, while VIX fell 11.21% to 15.84 and settled near its session low. There is no shallow-pullback, failed-retracement or session-extreme evidence to carry forward. Third, the weekend escalation that supports Stress is a supply-route story rather than observed index structure, and it is partly offset by Friday's 2.37% fall in crude on news of the Hormuz talks, by Saudi Arabia declining immediate retaliation at Baghdad's request, and by the Salalah meeting scheduled for Monday. A narrow danger window is published across the 22:00 UTC reopen hour and the hour that follows it, where thin liquidity can meet an unpriced weekend, rather than a broad session-wide caution. Existing-position management and emergency protection are unaffected by this mapping.
headline: Twenty-seven hours into the CME weekend halt the Nasdaq-100 still stands at its 29,368.44 Friday close with VIX 15.84, while the Saudi East-West pipeline carrying 4% to 5% of global oil supply stays shut and Houthi forces hold Perim island and the Bab el-Mandeb exit, leaving an unpriced supply-route weekend to meet Sunday's 22:00 UTC reopen three days before an FOMC decision priced near 87% for a hike.
body:
The price picture is unchanged, as a closed weekend requires, and every level was re-verified against primary sources this hour. The Nasdaq-100 quote page shows a 29,368.44 close, up 264.93 points or 0.91%, inside a 29,313.51 to 29,473.12 range against a 29,103.51 previous close, so the cash range spanned only 159.61 points and the close finished about 105 points below the high, roughly 4.5% under the 30,762.20 fifty-two-week high. On the week the Nasdaq fell about 0.7% and the S&P 500 about 0.6%, so Friday's 0.86% S&P gain and 509-point Dow advance snapped four losing sessions rather than establishing a trend. VIX is 15.84, down 2.00 points or 11.21% from 17.84, having settled near the 15.59 low of a 15.59 to 17.71 range. The latest H.15 observation, for 10 September, shows the 2-year at 4.56%, the 5-year at 4.75%, the 10-year at 4.95% and the 30-year at 5.37%, with the federal funds effective rate at 3.63%. WTI is marked $100.05, down 2.37% on the day but up 9.7% on the week and 20.15% on the month, with Brent $104.61, down 2.81%.

Two policy and supply threads define Stress. On policy, August CPI rose 0.4% on the month for a 3.4% annual rate in line with estimates, while core accelerated 0.3% on the month against a 0.2% estimate. Rate pricing responded far more than equities did: CME FedWatch pricing for a 25 basis point hike at Wednesday's decision stands near 87%, up from roughly 72% a day earlier and about 61% a week ago, which would take the target to 3.75%. On supply, Saudi Arabia shut its 1,200-kilometre East-West pipeline after drone strikes that Riyadh and Baghdad both attributed to Iraq-based origin, with satellite imagery showing a 60-mile smoke plume; the conduit normally moves 4% to 5% of global supply and had been the main route bypassing the disrupted Strait of Hormuz. Houthi forces seized Perim island, the port of Mocha and the coastal town of Dhubab, declaring navigation safe for all shipping except Saudi vessels, which places the Bab el-Mandeb exit under contest as well. Offsetting that, Saudi Arabia declined immediate retaliation at the Iraqi prime minister's request, and Iran, Iraq and Gulf states meet in Salalah on Monday to discuss Hormuz shipping, which is what halted crude's rally on Friday.

Delayed cross-asset context collected at 23:27 UTC is consistent with Friday's tape rather than with any live reading, and is treated accordingly: index futures last marked NQ up 0.86%, ES up 0.80% and YM up 0.93%, the VIX future down 8.41%, crude down 2.37% and gold effectively unchanged, with Treasury futures slightly lower across the curve. Participation was broad rather than narrow: seven of eight megacaps were higher with a mean gain near 0.94% though NVIDIA was flat, and five of seven semiconductors advanced with a mean near 1.75% led by Arm, Qualcomm, Intel and AMD. Broad but unled participation of that kind argues against the concentrated, one-way structure that would justify an elevated Tail reading. The same feed's calendar section was unavailable this hour, so the seven-day event list was built from the primary calendar instead.

Two genuine intra-horizon checkpoints exist, and neither can establish index structure. Tadawul opens at 07:00 UTC and closes near 12:00 UTC, providing the only live pricing anywhere of the pipeline shutdown and the Bab el-Mandeb seizure; as Saudi cash equity it informs Stress and Confidence without bearing on a Nasdaq-100 path. The CME reopen at 22:00 UTC is the first hour in which a path can form at all, and it is the reason the published danger window is confined to that hour and the one after it. Looking just beyond the horizon, pro forma Nasdaq-100 rebalance weights circulated late Friday point to a sizeable one-off passive adjustment at the 18 September close, effective 21 September, which is recorded as a calendar item rather than a current risk input. The conditional path published here drifts Tail from 6 to 19 through the closure, steps to 22 in the reopen hour and eases to 21 in the hour after it on the assumption that discovery is orderly; shallow pullbacks with repeated extension after the reopen would invalidate that assumption, and an orderly two-sided tape would let the estimate fall quickly.

lookbackSummary: All twenty-four clock-hours from 00:00 UTC to 23:00 UTC on 12 September carry a published Claude assessment, so every lookback slot is available and none is reconstructed. The window sits entirely inside the CME weekend closure. Tail opened at 5 and held a 5 to 6 band in normal mode across every slot, tracking the closure rather than any directional view, which is the correct behaviour for a score that measures price path when no price path exists. Stress decayed steadily from 60 to a 50 trough at 17:00 UTC as the initial pipeline shock was absorbed, then firmed through 52 and 53 to 57 in the final slot as the Bab el-Mandeb seizure, the attribution of the pipeline strikes and the jump in rate-hike pricing were each verified. Confidence held a narrow 85 to 87 range throughout. Every slot mapped to EA_ON and green, and no danger window was published in any of them.
outlookSummary: Twenty-two of the twenty-four forward slots lie inside the CME weekend closure that began at 21:00 UTC on Friday; the reference contract reopens at 22:00 UTC on Sunday, which is this horizon's twenty-third slot. Conditional Tail opens at 6 in the current slot, the only slot containing observed rather than hypothetical conditions, drifts gradually to 19 through the closure as unpriced weekend exposure accumulates, steps to 22 in the reopen hour and eases to 21 in the first full hour of discovery. Those two reopen slots map to WATCH and yellow; every other slot stays in the low band and maps to EA_ON and green. A narrow danger window is published across the reopen hour and the hour after it rather than a broad session-wide caution. Stress traces a shallow U, easing to 54 across the dead overnight hours and firming to 64 by the reopen as pre-positioning meets an unresolved supply picture and a near-certain Wednesday hike. Confidence dips to an 83 floor as Friday's verified levels age, then recovers to 87 once live quotes replace them. Two intra-horizon checkpoints carry information without establishing structure: the Tadawul open at 07:00 UTC gives the first live pricing of the supply shock, and the reopen auction is the first hour in which a Nasdaq-100 path can exist. Direction at the reopen is unassumed in either sign; the mechanism that would raise the estimate is a gap that holds without a meaningful retracement, and the one that would lower it is orderly two-sided discovery.
